statusDetail: Atomic coverage is structurally complete, but two consequential authenticated commerce checks are blocked. No score is published.

page.notes: Large public commerce MPA with homepage, search, product, authentication, WAF recovery, and protected checkout/account surfaces.

Rendered homepage DOM and computed styles

principleOutcomes.reason: A complete purchase requires an authenticated account, delivery details, and a real financial transaction. Search-to-product and add-to-cart were attempted, but the cart remained at zero in the anonymous test session; no real order was placed.

Checkout, cancellation, and account-management completion require authentication and potentially consequential account or financial changes. The public offer and sign-in entry were inspected, but those protected states were not executed.

paths.description: Homepage and global navigation, representing the merchandising gateway.
Search results for wireless headphones, representing listing, filtering, and product discovery.
Fire TV Stick 4K Max detail page, representing product media, specifications, reviews, and purchase controls.
Sign-in entry, representing authentication, autofill, passkeys, and invalid-input recovery.
Attempted add-to-cart and checkout journey. A real purchase and authenticated account changes were not performed.

findings.summary: The storefront ignores the user’s dark colour preference.
findings.evidence: Under prefers-color-scheme: dark, the search page remains white; the probe reports body rgb(255,255,255), color-scheme normal, and no prefers-color-scheme/light-dark() rules in readable CSS.
findings.suggestedFix: Declare color-scheme: light dark and provide preference-driven surface, text, border, and image treatments.

findings.summary: No explicit high-contrast or forced-colours adaptation was found.
findings.evidence: Readable CSS contained no prefers-contrast or forced-colors rules; control visibility therefore relies on the default palette rather than the user preference.
findings.suggestedFix: Add forced-colors and prefers-contrast treatments for essential controls and test them with platform high-contrast modes.

findings.summary: Overlay implementations rely on custom ARIA dialogs instead of native overlay primitives.
findings.evidence: The DOM/CSS probe found 25 role=dialog elements but zero <dialog>, popover, or <details> elements on the homepage.
findings.suggestedFix: Migrate transient UI to popover with light dismiss and modal flows to <dialog>; use <details> for disclosures.

findings.summary: Dense merchandising and navigation chrome competes with product content.
findings.evidence: Homepage, search, and product screenshots show stacked global nav, promotional strips, flyouts, carousels, and tightly packed cards occupying most of the first viewport.
findings.suggestedFix: Reduce competing promotional modules, reserve a clearer content hierarchy, and defer secondary chrome below the primary task.

findings.summary: Desktop pages are scaled down on narrow screens instead of reflowing.
findings.evidence: All three audited templates omit meta viewport. At 360x800, the browser uses a 1000 CSS-pixel layout scaled to 0.36; the homepage layout probe also measured 640px overflow.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a standards viewport meta tag and implement intrinsic, fluid template layouts that reflow at narrow widths.

findings.summary: Many interactive targets are too small for reliable touch input.
findings.evidence: On the product page, 191 of 228 visible interactive elements were below 44px in at least one dimension; many links were 14–20px high and several controls were 8x4px.
findings.suggestedFix: Provide at least 24x24 CSS pixels, preferably 44x44 for primary touch controls, with spacing and non-hover alternatives.

findings.summary: Largest Contentful Paint is outside the good range.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse measured 3.5s LCP and 3.5s FCP; the independent trace measured 2.28s LCP, showing variable but material startup cost.
findings.suggestedFix: Prioritise the actual LCP resource, reduce redirect/WAF startup cost, and defer non-critical work.

findings.summary: The homepage has a heavy, render-blocking delivery path.
findings.evidence: HAR recorded 108 requests and 2.37MB transferred, including 735KB fonts, 707KB scripts, five very-high-priority parser-inserted stylesheets, and a 291KB WAF challenge script.
findings.suggestedFix: Consolidate critical CSS, subset fonts, remove the redirect/challenge cost for legitimate clients, and defer non-critical assets.

findings.summary: The homepage ships avoidable unused code.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse estimated 124KiB unused JavaScript and 18KiB unused CSS.
findings.suggestedFix: Use route/template-level bundles, remove dead modules and duplicated styles, and load optional merchandising code on demand.

findings.summary: The product template exposes visible controls without reliable text alternatives.
findings.evidence: The product probe found 42 visible buttons, links, or submit inputs with no text, value, aria-label, or alt-derived name; the image audit also reported missing alt text.
findings.suggestedFix: Give every interactive control a programmatic name and meaningful images appropriate alt text; hide decorative media from assistive technology.

findings.summary: The homepage lacks a main landmark.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse’s landmark-one-main audit failed, and the DOM probe returned no <main> element on the homepage.
findings.suggestedFix: Wrap the unique page content in one <main> landmark and preserve the otherwise visible keyboard focus treatment.

findings.summary: Narrow-screen text is rendered as a miniature desktop page.
findings.evidence: At 360px the product and search templates retain a 1000px layout scaled to 0.36, making body copy, prices, and controls extremely small.
findings.suggestedFix: Fix viewport/reflow, then apply readable fluid type with comfortable line lengths and spacing.

findings.summary: The experience fails the reflow and target-size quality bar.
findings.evidence: Missing viewport metadata forces desktop-width scaling on all audited templates, while 191/228 product controls fall below 44px in one dimension.
findings.suggestedFix: Restore true mobile reflow, preserve user scaling, and enlarge touch targets without hiding content.

findings.summary: Image delivery lacks dimensions and modern responsive markup.
findings.evidence: The image audit found 45/46 images without width/height, 32 without srcset, and 45 legacy-format images.
findings.suggestedFix: Set intrinsic width/height or aspect-ratio, provide srcset/sizes, and serve AVIF/WebP where it reduces bytes.

findings.summary: Search results lack a meta description.
findings.evidence: The search probe found a descriptive title but no meta[name=description], while homepage and product templates did include descriptions.
findings.suggestedFix: Generate a concise, query-aware description for indexable result and listing templates.

findings.summary: Discovery signals include non-crawlable links and no viewport metadata.
findings.evidence: The homepage probe found prominent javascript:void(0) anchors, and homepage/search/product probes all found no viewport meta tag.
findings.suggestedFix: Use buttons for actions, real href links for navigation, and add a standards viewport declaration.

findings.summary: Listing/indexing signals are inconsistent.
findings.evidence: The search results page had no canonical URL, and /sitemap.xml returned HTTP 404; robots.txt otherwise allows ordinary public pages.
findings.suggestedFix: Publish a sitemap index and canonical URLs for stable listing/query variants while retaining deliberate private-route exclusions.

findings.summary: The audited product page exposes no JSON-LD product data.
findings.evidence: The product probe found zero application/ld+json blocks despite visible product, review, and offer content.
findings.suggestedFix: Publish accurate schema.org Product/Offer/AggregateRating JSON-LD and complete Open Graph metadata from visible data.

findings.summary: Core security headers are absent on the main response observed by Chrome.
findings.evidence: The headers primitive found HTTPS but no CSP, HSTS, X-Content-Type-Options, X-Frame-Options, Referrer-Policy, or Permissions-Policy.
findings.suggestedFix: Deploy a nonce/hash-based CSP, HSTS, nosniff, frame-ancestors, strict referrer policy, and a minimal Permissions-Policy.

findings.summary: The anonymous homepage has a broad telemetry and advertising request surface.
findings.evidence: Trackers/HAR recorded eight non-main origins and 104/108 requests classified as third-party by origin, including amazon-adsystem and telemetry endpoints; no exposed secrets were found.
findings.suggestedFix: Minimise anonymous telemetry, batch necessary events, document purposes, and defer advertising calls until justified by consent and user value.

findings.summary: Browser-enforced defensive policies are not configured.
findings.evidence: Neither CSP/frame-ancestors nor legacy X-Frame-Options was present, and HSTS, Referrer-Policy, and Permissions-Policy were also missing.
findings.suggestedFix: Add layered browser policies at the edge and verify them on normal, WAF, sign-in, and error responses.

findings.summary: Most homepage images use legacy formats without responsive candidates.
findings.evidence: The image audit found 45 legacy images, zero modern-format images, 32 without srcset, and 25 below-fold images without lazy loading.
findings.suggestedFix: Generate modern responsive variants, include srcset/sizes, reserve dimensions, and lazy-load non-critical below-fold media.

findings.summary: Anonymous loading performs substantial non-content work.
findings.evidence: The HAR shows 108 requests, including telemetry, ad-system calls, and a 291KB WAF script; 2.08MB of 2.37MB transferred came from non-main origins.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove or defer non-essential background work, batch telemetry, and avoid challenge code for already-validated low-risk sessions.

findings.summary: Third-party, font, and media weight is disproportionate before interaction.
findings.evidence: The anonymous homepage transfers 2.37MB: 735KB fonts, 522KB images, and 2.08MB from non-main origins before the user acts.
findings.suggestedFix: Set template budgets, subset and consolidate fonts, defer below-fold media, and cap third-party startup bytes.

findings.summary: Agentic commerce capabilities are not exposed and major AI agents are explicitly blocked.
findings.evidence: No WebMCP/agent tool registration was found, while robots.txt disallows GPTBot, ClaudeBot, OAI-SearchBot, ChatGPT-User, and GoogleAgent-Shopping.
findings.suggestedFix: If agentic commerce is intended, expose scoped WebMCP tools and a deliberate agent access policy with user confirmation for consequential actions.

findings.summary: The product template has a large in-memory footprint.
findings.evidence: The baseline heap summary contained about 904k heap nodes, 3.39m edges, 54.2MB self size, 66.5k closures, and 6,313 live DOM elements.
findings.suggestedFix: Reduce DOM/card duplication, release unused media/widget state, and lazy-initialise below-fold review and comparison modules.
